newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA LOSE SLATER, TRAIL INDIA BY 159.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA LOSE SLATER, TRAIL INDIA BY 159.

text.p: Australia suffered an early
setback in their second innings when they lost Michael Slater,
top scorer in their first innings, for nought on the third day
of the single test against India on Saturday.
Australia, who dismissed India for 361, were 20 for one at
lunch, still 159 behind.
India's debutant medium-pacer David Johnson earned his first
test wicket in the second over when Slater fiddled with a
delivery outside the off-stump and Mohammed Azharuddin at first
slip took a brilliant catch.
Ricky Ponting was lucky to survive a confident caught-behind
appeal before opening his score off Johnson.
The ball seemed to have touched Ponting's gloves before
travelling to wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia but umpire Peter Willey
refused the appeal which would have given Johnson his second
wicket in one over.
Mongia, who was the eighth Indian batsman out after scoring
152, erased former Australian captain Ian Chappell's record
highest score in any test between India and Australia at New
Delhi.
Mongia faced 365 balls during his 497-minute innings which
contained 18 fours and one six.
Chappell was watching from the television commentary box as
his score of 138 in 1969 venue was beaten by Mongia, who was
later bowled through the gate by Paul Reiffel.
Reiffel claimed three for 35 and was the most successful
Australian bowler.
